text:
alex: Prod canary for model-puller spiking 504s talking to S3 via privatelink in eu-west-1. Started ~09:02 UTC.
maya: seeing the same on canary-2, logs show connection reset. only affects calls to regional S3.
alex: I traced traffic — DNS for `s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` resolving to public IPs from the canary VPC, so requests are hitting NAT instead of the interface endpoint.
priya: @maya can you paste `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=service-name,Values=com.amazonaws.eu-west-1.s3` for the VPC?
maya: output: `VpcEndpointId: vpce-0f12ab34, State: available, DnsEntries: [s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com], NetworkInterfaces: [eni-0aa1bb2c]`
maya: checked route tables — no blackhole. But `route53resolver` associations might be the culprit.
maya: running:```bash
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0def3456
# returned empty
```
alex: aha — resolver rule for shared privatelink resolver not associated to this VPC, so VPC DNS isn't forwarding to shared resolver -> fallback public DNS -> public IPs -> NAT egress.
sre-bot: Alert: NAT gw conntrack usage > 90% in eu-west-1 (metric).
tom: NAT conntrack exhaustion would explain resets. Why didn't automation associate the resolver rule during account onboarding?
priya: I looked at the onboarding run logs, and the iam role used in account-222 had `route53resolver:AssociateResolverRule` denied due to a missing principal condition. Automation quietly skipped without failing pipeline.
jon: quick mitigation: manually associate resolver rule and restart canary pods. Also put a short-lived host route to prefer ENI? (keeping it simple: resolver rule association).
maya: did manual association:```bash
aws route53resolver associate-resolver-rule --resolver-rule-id rslvr-1234abcd --vpc-id vpc-0def3456
```
maya: pods re-resolved `s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` to the VPC endpoint IPs, success rate went back up to 99% in 30s.
alex: nice. longer term we should: 1) fail loudly in onboarding if resolver assoc fails, 2) add automation test that validates `dig s3...` in each VPC, 3) add alert if resolver-rule associations drift.
priya: also add a guardrail: if resolver missing, don't allow canary traffic to default to NAT (or throttle it) — or at least spike alerts on NAT conntrack.
jon: I've created a short RFC for the onboarding fix and added a ticket to increase NAT capacity temporarily and tune conntrack on the NAT fleet.
tom: can we also audit endpoint security groups? one of our past issues was SGs referencing cross-account SG ids and they'd be silently ignored causing traffic drops.
alex: good call — let's add SG check to the onboarding lint. For this incident the SG on vpce-0f12ab34 allowed 443 from the VPC CIDR, so not the SG here.
sre-bot: Incident resolved: root cause — resolver rule not associated to secondary VPC due to IAM deny in onboarding automation -> DNS fell back to public -> NAT conntrack exhausted -> connection resets. Remediations: manual assoc, onboarding RBAC fix, telemetry/alerts for resolver associations and NAT conntrack.
maya: thanks all. monitoring looks green now :thumbsup:
jon: filing post-incident notes and runbook updates.
priya: great, closing the loop.
